### Load environment

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(broom)
library(ggrepel)
```

```{r}
data_dir <- here("data")

augment_df <- readr::read_tsv(file = file.path(data_dir,
                                                "03_dat_aug.tsv.gz"),
                              col_names = TRUE,
                              show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Manual differential expression analysis

To uncover what genes are up- or downregulated based on different stratifications such as: age groups, race, vital status etc.

### DEA stratified on vital status

We convert the condition (vital status) to a binary vector and then group the dataframe by gene_names, obtaining tibbles with paired expression values and vital status of the source per gene. We remove observations with a vital status of "Unknown".

```{r}
vital_df <- augment_df |>
  select(gene_name, log2_tpm, vital_status) |> 
  filter(vital_status != "Unknown") |> 
  mutate(vital_status = case_when(vital_status == "Dead" ~ 0,
                                  vital_status == "Alive" ~ 1)) |> 
  group_by(gene_name) |> 
  nest()
```

We apply a linear model to each nested gene, and extract statistics using a default alpha-level threshold of 5%.

```{r}
model_nest_df <- vital_df |> 
  mutate(model_object = map(.x = data,
                            .f = ~ lm(formula = log2_tpm ~ vital_status,
                                      data = .x)),
         model_object_tidy = map(.x = model_object,
                                 .f = ~ tidy(x = .x,
                                             conf.int = TRUE)))
```

We extract the statistics of interest and apply an FDR correction for the adjusted p-value as we now consider the unnested data.

```{r}
model_vital_df <- model_nest_df |> 
  unnest(model_object_tidy) |> 
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |> 
  select(gene_name, p.value, estimate, conf.low, conf.high) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(
    p.adj = p.adjust(p = p.value, method = "fdr"),
    significant = p.adj < 0.05
  ) |> 
  arrange(p.adj)
```

```{r}
slice_min(model_vital_df, p.adj, n= 10)
```

#### Visualizations

```{r}
forest_plot <- model_vital_df |>
  slice_min(p.adj, n = 15) |>
  mutate(gene_name = fct_reorder(gene_name, estimate)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, 
             y = gene_name,
             color = p.adj)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, 
             linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "gray50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf.low, 
                    xmax = conf.high),
                width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Differentially Expressed Genes: Alive vs Dead vital status",
       subtitle = "Genes of lowest FDR (BeatAML1.0-COHORT)",
       x = expression(log[2] ~ "Fold Change (95% CI)"),
       y = NULL,
       color = "FDR (5%)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

forest_plot
```

```{r}
volcano_plot <- model_vital_df |>
  mutate(neg_log10_p = -log10(p.value),
         label = if_else(p.value < 0.05 & abs(estimate) > 1, 
                         gene_name, NA_character_)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, 
             y = neg_log10_p, 
             color = p.value < 0.05)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, 
             size = 1.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), 
             linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "gray60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), 
             linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "gray60") +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label),
                  color = "black",
                  size = 3.5,
                  max.overlaps = 15,
                  na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "steelblue", 
                                "TRUE" = "maroon"),
                     labels = c("FALSE" = "Not significant", 
                                "TRUE" = "p-value < 0.05")) +
  labs(title = "Volcano Plot: Alive vs Dead vital status",
       subtitle = "(BeatAML1.0-COHORT)",
       x = expression(log[2] ~ "Fold Change"),
       y = expression(-log[10] ~ "(p-value)"),
       color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

volcano_plot
```

### DEA stratified on ELN risk

Same pipeline is repeated on the data with ELN risk classification as stratifying factor.

```{r}
eln_df <- augment_df |>
  select(gene_name, log2_tpm, eln_risk_classification) |> 
  filter(eln_risk_classification %in% c("Adverse", "Favorable")) |> 
  mutate(eln_risk_classification = case_when(eln_risk_classification == "Adverse" ~ 0,
                                             eln_risk_classification == "Favorable" ~ 1)) |> 
  group_by(gene_name) |> 
  nest()
```

```{r}
eln_nest_df <- eln_df |> 
  mutate(model_object = map(.x = data,
                            .f = ~ lm(formula = log2_tpm ~ eln_risk_classification,
                                      data = .x)),
         model_object_tidy = map(.x = model_object,
                                 .f = ~ tidy(x = .x,
                                             conf.int = TRUE)))
```

```{r}
model_eln_df <- eln_nest_df |> 
  unnest(model_object_tidy) |> 
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |> 
  select(gene_name, p.value, estimate, conf.low, conf.high) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(
    p.adj = p.adjust(p = p.value, method = "fdr"),
    significant = p.adj < 0.05,
    FC = 2^abs(estimate),
  ) |> 
  relocate(FC, .before = conf.low) |> 
  arrange(p.adj)
```

```{r}
slice_min(model_eln_df, p.adj, n=10)
```

#### Visualizations

```{r}
forest_plot <- model_eln_df |>
  slice_min(p.adj, n = 15) |>
```

### Multivariate linear model to adjust for confounders

We test whether the top 5 significant genes found in the ELN risk classification analysis remain significant after adjusting for sex. The adjustment is obtained by the addition of linear terms based on these variables.

```{r}
eln_top5 <- model_eln_df |> 
  filter(significant) |> 
  pull(gene_name)


eln_confounder_df <- augment_df |>
  filter(eln_risk_classification %in% c("Adverse", "Favorable"),
         sex_at_birth %in% c("male", "female")) |> 
  select(gene_name, log2_tpm, vital_status, sex_at_birth, eln_risk_classification) |> 
  mutate(eln_risk_classification = case_when(eln_risk_classification == "Adverse" ~ 0,
                                             eln_risk_classification == "Favorable" ~ 1),
         sex_at_birth = case_when(sex_at_birth == "female" ~ 0,
                                  sex_at_birth == "male" ~ 1)) |> 
  group_by(gene_name) |> 
  nest()
```

```{r}
eln_confounder_nest_df <- eln_confounder_df |> 
  mutate(model_object = map(.x = data,
                            .f = ~ lm(formula = log2_tpm ~ eln_risk_classification + sex_at_birth,
                                      data = .x)),
         model_object_tidy = map(.x = model_object,
                                 .f = ~ tidy(x = .x,
                                             conf.int = TRUE)))
```

```{r}
model_eln_confounder_df <- eln_confounder_nest_df |> 
  unnest(model_object_tidy) |> 
  filter(term == "eln_risk_classification") |> 
  select(gene_name, p.value, estimate, conf.low, conf.high) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(p.adj = p.adjust(p = p.value, method = "fdr"),
         significant = p.adj < 0.05,
         FC = 2^abs(estimate)) |> 
  relocate(FC, .before = conf.low) |> 
  arrange(p.adj)
```

We investigate if genes remained significant

```{r}
eln_conf_top5_sig <- model_eln_confounder_df |> 
  filter(gene_name %in% eln_top5) |> 
  arrange(gene_name) |> 
  pull(significant,gene_name)

eln_top5_sig <- model_eln_df |> 
  filter(gene_name %in% eln_top5) |> 
  arrange(gene_name) |> 
  pull(significant, gene_name)

cat("Gene remained significant after adjusting for confounder:\n")
eln_top5_sig == eln_conf_top5_sig

```

#### PCA analysis to investigate potential confounder

It seems that sex may be a confounder. We explore this further by doing a visualization of the PCA modelled data, and investigate whether any sex based clusters surface. We use the 1000 most variable genes.

```{r}
top1000_var <- augment_df |> 
  group_by(gene_id) |> 
  summarize(gene_var = var(log2_tpm)) |> 
  slice_max(gene_var, n = 1000) |> 
  pull(gene_id)

pca_meta <- augment_df |> 
  filter(gene_id %in% top1000_var) |>
  distinct(sample_id, sex_at_birth)
```

```{r}
augment_df_wider <- augment_df |> 
  select(gene_id,
         log2_tpm,
         sample_id) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample_id,
              values_from =log2_tpm) |>
  filter(gene_id %in% top1000_var) |> 
  column_to_rownames("gene_id")
```

```{r}
pca <- prcomp(t(augment_df_wider),
              center = TRUE,
              scale = TRUE)

var_explained <- (pca$sdev^2) / sum(pca$sdev^2)

pca$x |>
  as.data.frame() |> 
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_id") |> 
  select(sample_id, PC1, PC2) |> 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = PC1,
                       y = PC2,
                       color = pca_meta$sex_at_birth)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "PCA of Top 1,000 Most Variable Genes",
       subtitle = "(BeatAML1.0-COHORT)",
       x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", var_explained[1] * 100),
       y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", var_explained[2] * 100),
       color = "Sex") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

No clear clusters appear in the latent space visualization of the two princaple components with largest variacne explained when samples are stratified by sex. It could be that these are captured within lower-order components, however that also means a lower variance effect, and it most likely not being a confounder. There could still be non-linear relationships that this linear projection cannot capture.
